title: Origins and History of Dishwasher (Hand-Crank/Early)
body:
The Dishwasher (Hand-Crank/Early) belongs to the 1886–1950s era and traces to Josephine Cochrane.

The icebox (insulated cabinet + block ice, iceman's daily round) ruled until mechanical refrigeration: Kelvinator (1918), Frigidaire (1918, GM), and GE's Monitor Top (1927) electrified cold. Wringer washers (1900s–40s) mechanized washday's worst labor; Bendix's automatic (1937) finished it. The vacuum cleaner (Hoover, 1908) and electric iron replaced carpet beaters and sadirons. Toasters (1909 pop-up, 1926 automatic), fans, and mixers (KitchenAid, 1919) filled kitchens. Rural electrification (1930s REA) spread them; postwar suburbia standardized them.

Within that longer story, Dishwasher (Hand-Crank/Early): The 1886 patent; the 1893's. The Cochrane is the dish's washer.

title: How Dishwasher (Hand-Crank/Early) Works
body:
Early refrigerators compressed refrigerant (sulfur dioxide, then Freon-12 from 1930) in a vapor-compression cycle: compress, condense, expand, evaporate — moving heat from inside the box to the kitchen. Wringer washers agitated in a tub and squeezed water through rollers (fingers beware). Vacuum cleaners used motor-driven suction and beater bars; the Hoover's bag was the filter. Toasters timed nichrome elements; automatic pop-ups used bimetallic or clockwork release.

Applied to the Dishwasher (Hand-Crank/Early) (1886–1950s, Josephine Cochrane): The Cochrane is the dish's washer.

The engineering principles above are exactly what made this class of technology practical: every unit is a working compromise between materials, energy, precision, and cost.

title: Dishwasher (Hand-Crank/Early) in Culture
body:
The icebox had a drip pan and a card in the window ('50 lbs today'); the wringer washer had a washday that owned Monday. The Monitor Top hummed in the kitchen corner; the Hoover hung in the closet. Appliances were dowry, status, and liberation — 'washday blues' ended with the automatic. Harvest gold and avocado are the colors of memory.

The Dishwasher (Hand-Crank/Early) carries that cultural charge directly: The Cochrane is the dish's washer.

title: Collecting and Preserving Dishwasher (Hand-Crank/Early)

Monitor Tops and round Frigidaires are the grails — check compressors. Wringer washers need space and caution. Toasters (Toastmaster, Sunbeam T-20) are affordable and usable. Hoover 28s and Kirby classics clean. Always rewire cloth cords; check refrigerant legality before servicing sealed systems.

For the Dishwasher (Hand-Crank/Early) specifically: 1886's Cochrane: the 1886 — the 1950s'.. Prioritize completeness and originality over shine; a working Dishwasher (Hand-Crank/Early) with honest wear outranks a polished non-runner.

title: Dishwasher (Hand-Crank/Early) — Refrigeration cycle + washday estimator (Runnable Python)
body:
Computes ideal vapor-compression COP and estimates icebox ice-melt and washday water heating — the thermodynamics of the historic home.

The program below is real, runnable Python 3. Save it as demo.py and run `python3 demo.py`. It models the core mathematics of the Dishwasher (Hand-Crank/Early) so you can experiment with the parameters yourself.
code:
# Historic home thermodynamics (public-domain formulas)
def carnot_cop(t_cold_c, t_hot_c):
    tc, th = t_cold_c + 273.15, t_hot_c + 273.15
    return tc / (th - tc)

print(f"ideal COP (4C inside, 32C kitchen): {carnot_cop(4, 32):.1f}")
print("(real 1930s machines: ~1-2; the ideal taunts the engineer)")

# Icebox: 50 lb block, latent heat 144 BTU/lb -> cooling delivered
ice_lb = 50
btu = ice_lb * 144
print(f"\n50-lb ice block delivers {btu:,} BTU of cooling as it melts")

# Heating wash water: 20 gal from 50F to 140F
gal, dT_F = 20, 90
btu_needed = gal * 8.34 * dT_F
print(f"heating 20 gal wash water 90F: {btu_needed:,.0f} BTU")
print(f"  = {btu_needed/3412:.1f} kWh electric, or ~{btu_needed/20000:.1f} lb coal equivalent")
